string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the country\'s four direct-administered municipalities. With a history spanning more than three millennia, it served as the final imperial capital during the Ming and Qing dynasties and is home to iconic UNESCO World Heritage Sites including the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven and the Summer Palace. As the nation\'s political, cultural and educational centre, Beijing hosts the headquarters of major state institutions, leading universities and national cultural organisations. It is also a modern global city that hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, becoming the first city to hold both events.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city and a direct-administered municipality on the central coast, at the mouth of the Yangtze River. Long the nation\'s busiest port and commercial gateway, it blends a colonial Bund waterfront with the futuristic skyscrapers of Pudong\'s Lujiazui skyline. As China\'s financial and trade hub, Shanghai hosts the Shanghai Stock Exchange, multinational corporations and the annual China International Import Expo. Its economy spans finance, manufacturing, technology and logistics, while its dense urban centre is known for its museums, art galleries, cuisine and the historic Yu Garden. It remains the symbol of China\'s rapid modernisation.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwest China, sitting at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers in the Sichuan Basin. Known for its steep, hilly terrain and foggy winters, it is often called a mountain city and a bridge capital, with multi-level roads and dramatic river views. It became China\'s fourth municipality in 1997, governing a vast, densely populated territory that includes large rural areas. Chongqing is an industrial and transport hub, famous for its heavy industry, automobile manufacturing and Yangtze River cruise trade, and it is the culinary home of fiery Sichuan hotpot.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, located on the Bohai Bay roughly 120 kilometres southeast of Beijing. Founded along the Grand Canal, it grew into a major northern treaty port and industrial centre, and its historic Five Great Avenues district preserves European-style colonial architecture. Today Tianjin is a key port, logistics and manufacturing city, home to the large Tianjin Port and the Binhai New Area economic zone. It hosts several prominent universities and is known for its street humour, traditional mahua snacks and the waterfront skyline along the Hai River.
